reason: Every rule in this entry identifies a specific type assertion construct (double cast, non-null assertion, narrowing as-cast, Kotlin !!, Go single-value type assertion) that overrides the type checker without a runtime check, and the rule text says what is wrong in each case.

Every rule identifies a specific annotation or cast that gives a value an opaque or top type (as any, Record<string, unknown>, object, bare dict, Array<any>) where the code depends on a structure the type checker can no longer see, and the rule text says what is wrong.

Each rule identifies a domain concept carried as a raw primitive (stringly-typed parameter, primitive obsession, stringly-typed cross-file value, type invariant design gap) where the type does not encode the constrained value set, and the rule text states what the failure is.

condition: the set of variants being dispatched over is closed (a discriminated union or exhaustive enum), not an open hierarchy or externally defined value set
reason: Both rules find dispatch sites (match/switch, isinstance/elif chains) that lack exhaustiveness enforcement, but the failure belongs to this family only if the variant set is closed; neither rule checks that condition.

Every rule identifies a specific construct that suppresses an adopted check rather than satisfying it: inline TS directives, lint escape directives, build config warning suppression, linter config modification, and unjustified lint suppression. Each rule text says what is wrong.
The single rule identifies a concrete mismatch where a consumer's declared type contradicts the shape the producing endpoint actually sends, and the rule text states what the failure is.

Both rules identify a published signature that exposes a type not part of the boundary contract (an ORM entity leaked through an API, or a private type referenced by an export), and the rule text says what is wrong.

The rule counts escape-hatch annotations as a ratio of all type annotations in a file and flags files exceeding thirty per cent with at least five annotations; it names no individual defective construct and selects files for review by a ratio.
